newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's stock market ends session lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's stock market ends session lower.

text.p: The Casablanca bourse closed on Tuesday lower pulled down by the market's largest companies, including Societe Nationale d'Investissement, traders said.
The all-share index closed at 435.89 points, down 0.68 percent compared with 438.88 points on Monday.
"SNI and BCM bank shares drop was the main factor behind the bourse index decline," a broker said.
SNI, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate, lost 10 dirhams in one session to close at 560 dirhams.
The firm was expected to announce for the first time its consolidated results for 1995, a market analyst said.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc (BCM), the market largest capitalisation lost one dirhams to close at 694 dirhams.
ONA, the country's largest private group, after a significant rise last week, remained stable at 510 dirhams.
Wafabank, one of the market liquid stocks gained three dirhams to close at 303 dirhams.

The bank has a market capitalisation of 2.7 billion dirhams and registered a liquidity rate of 8.2 percent in the first half of the year, one of the highest rates on the market, an analyst at Wafa Bourse said.
The traded volume was 25.4 million dirhams, up from 11.6 million on Monday's session.
